title: Reviewing a diff: sources, sinks and the questions to ask
summary: A security review is not a checklist read aloud. Follow each input from where it enters to where it is used, ask the four questions on every new endpoint, and spot the bug in real-looking diffs before fixing one.

steps.title: Sources, sinks, and what sits between them
body: Almost every bug in this topic has the same shape: data from a **source** reaches a **sink** without the right check in between.
| Sources (attacker-controlled) | Sinks (dangerous when fed attacker data) | The check in between |
| route values, query, body, headers, cookies | SQL text: `FromSqlRaw`, `ExecuteSqlRaw`, `CommandText` | parameters |
| uploaded files and their names | `Process.Start`, `sh -c` | no shell, `ArgumentList`, validation |
| data stored by other users (reviews, names) | HTML: `Html.Raw`, `innerHTML`, string-built pages | encoding, sanitizing |
| webhooks, partner APIs, queue messages | `HttpClient.GetAsync(url)` | allow-list, IP check |
| JWT claims you did not verify | `Path.Combine`, `File.*`, `Results.File` | resolve and confine |
| | database lookups by id | ownership checks |

Four questions for every new or changed endpoint: **Who can call this?** (authentication, the right policy) **Which object does it touch, and is it theirs?** (object-level) **What goes in?** (each input to each sink) **What comes out?** (fields, errors, headers). Most findings fall out of those four.

steps.prompt: Review this diff. What is the most important comment?
code: + app.MapGet("/api/receipts/{id:int}", async (int id, ShopDb db, ClaimsPrincipal user) =>
+     return receipt is null ? Results.NotFound() : Results.Ok(receipt);
options: Any signed-in user can read any receipt: filter by the caller's id (and return a DTO, not the entity)
The route needs a version prefix
steps.explain: Authenticated, but not authorized for *this* receipt: classic BOLA. Returning the entity also publishes every column the table gets in the future.

code: +     return Results.Ok(new { next = f.ReturnUrl ?? "/" });   // back to where the user was
options: An open redirect: a phishing link with returnUrl=https://evil.example sends users to a fake page after a real sign-in. Allow only local paths
Nothing: the user typed their own password
steps.explain: Open redirects (CWE-601) make phishing convincing: the link really is your domain. Accept only paths that start with a single `/` (not `//` or `/\`), the rule `Url.IsLocalUrl` implements in MVC.

steps.prompt: Lines from different pull requests. Which deserve a security comment?

steps.title: Writing the comment
body: A security review comment that gets fixed has four parts: **what** can happen, **how** (a concrete request), **the fix**, and **how bad**. For example:
Blocking: any signed-in user can read any receipt.
Fix: FirstOrDefaultAsync(r => r.Id == id && r.UserId == userId), 404 otherwise,
Severity: high (personal data, every customer, trivial to exploit).

Be specific, be kind, and mark what blocks the merge. "Looks insecure?" gets ignored; a request someone can paste into a terminal does not. And add the test: a regression test with the attack request is the review's most durable output.

steps.title: Fix PR #904 before it merges
prompt: The PR adds receipts and a return URL after sign-in. `X-User` stands in for the session. Fix both comments:
1. `GET /receipts/{id}`: only the owner may read a receipt (`404` otherwise), and the answer is `{ id, total }` only: no `paymentToken`.

2. `POST /login` answers `{ "next": ... }`: `returnUrl` is used only when it is a **local path**: it starts with `/`, and the second character is neither `/` nor `\`. Anything else (absolute URLs, `//evil.example`, `/\evil.example`, empty) gives `"/"`.
starter: var receipts = new List<Receipt> { new(5001, "ada", 49.00m, "tok_ada_1"), new(5002, "bob", 12.00m, "tok_bob_2") };
return r is null ? Results.NotFound() : Results.Ok(r);
if (f.Password != "correct horse battery staple") return Results.Unauthorized();
record Receipt(int Id, string Owner, decimal Total, string PaymentToken);
record LoginForm(string Username, string Password, string? ReturnUrl);
solution: var receipts = new List<Receipt> { new(5001, "ada", 49.00m, "tok_ada_1"), new(5002, "bob", 12.00m, "tok_bob_2") };
// Local paths only: "/orders" yes; "//evil.example", "/\\evil.example" and "https://..." no.
if (Caller(ctx) is not { } user) return Results.Unauthorized();
var r = receipts.FirstOrDefault(x => x.Id == id && x.Owner == user);
return r is null ? Results.NotFound() : Results.Ok(new { r.Id, r.Total });
if (f.Password != "correct horse battery staple") return Results.Unauthorized();
record Receipt(int Id, string Owner, decimal Total, string PaymentToken);
record LoginForm(string Username, string Password, string? ReturnUrl);
hints: Receipts: add `&& x.Owner == user` and return `new { r.Id, r.Total }`.
template: {{CODE}}
static class DojoTests
static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Get(HttpClient http, string url, string user)
var msg = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, url);
msg.Headers.Add("X-User", user);
return http.SendAsync(msg);
static async Task<string?> Next(HttpClient http, string? returnUrl) =>
DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/login", new { username = "ada", password = "correct horse battery staple", returnUrl })), "next");
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("Receipts could be checked", async () =>
var own = await Get(http, "/receipts/5001", "ada");
DojoWeb.Status("ada reads her receipt", 200, own);
var body = await DojoWeb.Text(own);
Dojo.Check("...without the payment token", !body.Contains("tok_") && !body.Contains("paymentToken", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase), body);
Dojo.Eq("...with its total", "49.00", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(await Get(http, "/receipts/5001", "ada")), "total"));
DojoWeb.Status("bob cannot read ada's receipt", 404, await Get(http, "/receipts/5001", "bob"));
await Dojo.TryAsync("The return URL could be checked", async () =>
Dojo.Eq("a local path is kept", "/orders/1001", await Next(http, "/orders/1001"));
Dojo.Eq("no returnUrl gives /", "/", await Next(http, null));
Dojo.Eq("an absolute URL gives /", "/", await Next(http, "https://evil.example/login"));
Dojo.Eq("a protocol-relative URL gives /", "/", await Next(http, "//evil.example"));
Dojo.Eq("/\\evil.example gives /", "/", await Next(http, "/\\evil.example"));
Dojo.Eq("javascript: gives /", "/", await Next(http, "javascript:alert(1)"));
